title: What Does Incognito Mode Actually Hide?
sources: Google Chrome Help, 'Browse in Incognito mode' (support.google.com/chrome/answer/95464) and 'How Chrome Incognito keeps your browsing private' (support.google.com/chrome/answer/9845881): Chrome won't save browsing history, cookies and site data, or information entered in forms; your activity might still be visible to websites you visit, your employer or school, or your internet service provider; downloads and bookmarks are kept

Mozilla, 'Incognito browser: What it really means' (mozilla.org/en-US/technology/incognito-browser): private browsing deletes local history and cookies when you close the window, but does not hide your IP address or your activity from your ISP, employer or the sites you visit

ABC News / AP, 'Google to delete billions of browser records to settle Incognito lawsuit' (April 2024, Brown v. Google): Google agreed to destroy billions of data records reflecting users' private browsing activity

lines.text: What does incognito mode actually hide?
When you open a private window,
your browser starts a fresh, empty session,
and when you close it, it throws it all away:
lines.caps: AND WHEN YOU *CLOSE IT | IT *THROWS | IT ALL *AWAY

lines.text: your history, your cookies, and whatever you typed into forms.
So the next person on that laptop sees nothing.
your school or office Wi-Fi, and your internet provider,
can still see which sites you visit,
and websites still see your IP address.
Google even agreed in twenty twenty-four
to delete billions of records from private browsing.
Incognito hides you from your laptop, not from the internet.
